chunks: From him, from al-Naḍr, from Ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: If a man does not find means of purification and he is junub, then let him wipe from the earth and perform salat (prayer). Then when he finds water, let him perform ghusl (ritual bath), and his salat (prayer) which he performed has sufficed him.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَتْهُ: it has sufficed him, meaning it fulfilled the legal requirement
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth, used as the medium for tayammum
key_terms.جُنُبًا: in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.طَهُورًا: a means of ritual purification, here referring to purifying water
key_terms.فَلْيَمْسَحْ: let him wipe, referring here to tayammum with earth

ai.seo_question: If a junub person performs tayammum and prays without water, must the salat (prayer) be repeated after finding water?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for a junub person who cannot find water: he performs tayammum using the earth and then performs salat (prayer). If he later finds water, he performs ghusl, but the salat (prayer) already performed is valid and does not require repetition.
